role.altitude: The week is still the yard, the customer, the sprinkler layout, and the fee she will say out loud. She stops hunting a stored equipment list, a stored price range, and a rate card. She does not gain a right to let a list recommend, a calculation install, or a draft set the fee.
skills_to_grow: Leave a blank equipment list unread and recommend from the yard
Answer from the office sheet when the stored price range is blank
Figure coverage on paper when the head-flow table is blank
Refuse a fee the rate card does not support
role.ambitious_version: She still recommends, answers, designs and negotiates. A blank rate stays blank until she names the fee, and a coverage figure she rejects is hers to recompute.

steps.what: List the stored grounds equipment for this crew.
Notice the working conditions that slow this crew.
Decide which change would increase crew efficiency.
Recommend that equipment change to the crew.

tasks.design: {DOCS} lists the stored grounds equipment for the site before she walks it. She still notices the working conditions, decides the change, and recommends it to the crew. The list does not recommend, does not fill a sheet, and does not send an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The equipment list sat in a binder, so she walked the yard before she could name what the crew already has.
tasks.enabler_now: A document store can list stored equipment before she walks the site. The recommendation is still her judgement.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see which condition slows this crew. A list cannot tell her that.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can tell whether a mower change would help this crew on this ground.
tasks.altitude: She still walks the yard and still recommends the change. She stops searching for an equipment list that is already on file. She does not gain a right to let the list speak for her.

reach.task: Use the equipment she recommended on this site.
reach.learn: Which equipment the list already names, so a blank list is not treated as a known machine.

evidence.claim: Where the Dutch works-council rule applies, clock-in or inspection results tied to a named cleaner can check attendance or performance and need consent. This list is equipment on a site. It does not record how a named worker performed.
An AI scheduler that allocates shifts from behaviour or traits, or that scores workers, is high-risk under Annex III 4(b). This list does not allocate shifts and does not score the crew.
An automated decision with a significant effect needs a person who can intervene. Recommending the change is her speech after the walk. The list does not take it.
The range is a scenario for a recommendation she still has to make on site. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The equipment card has site id, equipment name, and whether it is on that site. The producer is whoever keeps the grounds equipment list, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If the site id is blank or the list names the wrong site, the list step does not run and she recommends from what she sees in the yard. A blank is not filled with a guess.
Noticing the conditions, deciding the change, and recommending it stay at full time. The only shortened step is hunting equipment that is already listed.
The list does not recommend, does not fill a sheet, and does not send an alert. It does not score a worker and does not record attendance.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the office when the list names the wrong site. That telling is her own speech. The list does not send it.
unknowns: Whether this firm keeps grounds equipment as a stored list with a site id, or only as labels on the machines.
Whether this workplace is covered by the Dutch works-council rule.
research_questions: On a week of site walks, how often is the equipment list filled for that site before she leaves the yard office?
How often does the stored list name a machine that is not the one on the ground?

incremental.description: Tell the office when the stored equipment list names the wrong site. The list does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the site id and the equipment names are already stored, she skips hunting the binder. When the list is blank or names the wrong site, she recommends from the yard and the saving is zero. Noticing the conditions, deciding the change, and recommending it are not shortened.

tasks.short: Answer method, material and price inquiries.

steps.what: List stored methods, materials and price ranges for this inquiry.
Read the inquiry from current or prospective customers.
Answer customers on those methods, materials and price ranges.

tasks.design: {DOCS} and the {SPREADSHEET} list the stored methods, materials and price ranges for the service named in the inquiry. She still reads the inquiry in {EMAIL} and answers the customers herself. The list does not answer, does not send a message, and does not raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Method sheets and price ranges sat in different folders, so she hunted them before she could answer.
tasks.enabler_now: The stored method and the stored price range can be listed beside the inquiry. She still speaks the answer.
tasks.still_hard: A prospective customer asks about a site she has not seen. The list cannot price that.
tasks.human_edge: She hears what the customer wants and says what the firm will and will not do.
tasks.altitude: She still answers the customer. She stops hunting a method sheet and a price range that are already stored. She does not gain a right to let a list or a draft reply for her.

reach.task: Bring the materials the answer named for that job.
reach.learn: Which method and material the stored card states, so a blank range is not treated as a quoted price.

evidence.claim: Suite MKB, a package for landscapers, keeps planning, calculations from work packages, and quotes. Listing a stored method and a stored price range is that kind of stored quote. The advertorial does not measure time saved, and the package is not claimed to answer the customer.
The range is a scenario for inquiries whose price range is already on the sheet. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The price card has service name, method name, material name, price-range low and price-range high. The producer is whoever filed the method sheet and the price list, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If a price range or a method is blank, the list does not invent a figure and she answers from the office sheet. A blank is not a quote.
Reading the inquiry and answering the customers stay at full time. The only shortened step is hunting a method and a range that are already stored.
The list does not answer, does not send a message, and does not raise an alert. There is no chatbot and no drafted reply.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the office when a stored range is for the wrong service. That telling is her own speech. The list does not send it.
unknowns: Whether method sheets and price ranges are stored as fields, or still paper in the yard office.
How often a prospective customer asks about a site that has no stored service name.
research_questions: On a week of inquiries, how often are method, material and price range filled before she picks up the phone?
How often is the stored range for a different service than the one the customer asked about?

incremental.description: Tell the office when a stored price range is for the wrong service. The list does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the service name, method, material and price range are already stored, she skips hunting the folders. When any of those is blank, or the customer describes a site with no stored service, she answers from the office sheet and the saving is zero. Reading the inquiry and answering are not shortened.

steps.what: Record the measured water pressure and valve points.
Calculate sprinkler coverage from those site measures.
Check that coverage still meets the installation needs she measured.
Design the sprinkler systems layout for that ground.
Supervise installation of those sprinkler systems.

tasks.design: She records the area, the water pressure and the valve points first. A {SPREADSHEET} then calculates sprinkler coverage from those measures and the stored head-flow table, and she checks the figures against the ground before she marks the layout and supervises the installation. The calculation writes those coverage figures. It does not raise an alert and does not send the layout.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coverage was figured by hand from a head-flow table she had to find, after she had already measured the ground.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she has written the measures, a sheet can apply the stored head-flow table. She still checks the ground and supervises the install.
tasks.still_hard: Pressure at the tap and the shape of the beds are on site. The sheet cannot see them.
tasks.human_edge: She stands on the ground and will not install a layout that misses a bed she can see.
tasks.altitude: She still measures, still marks the layout, and still supervises the install. She stops doing the coverage arithmetic when the head-flow table and her measures are both present. She does not gain a right to let the sheet design or install.

reach.task: Lay the pipe and heads the layout marks.
reach.learn: Which valve points her layout names, so a blank measure is not treated as a finished design.

evidence.claim: No source in this digest shows a product calculating sprinkler coverage. The range is a scenario for a site where the head-flow table is already stored. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Her measure note, written in the first step, has area in square metres, water pressure at the tap, and the valve points. That writing is inside this task and stays at full time.
The head-flow table has head model, flow per head and radius. The producer is whoever filed that table, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If the table is blank or her measures are blank, the calculation does not run and she figures coverage while she designs. The sheet does not invent a pressure or a radius.
Measuring, checking the figures against the beds, marking the layout, and supervising the installation stay at full time. The only shortened step is the arithmetic when both inputs exist.
The calculation writes the coverage figures on the sheet. It does not raise an out-of-range alert and does not send the layout. A later change to the measures means she does not use those figures.
unknowns: Whether this firm has a head-flow table with flow and radius per head, or only a paper catalogue.
How often the pressure at the tap differs from the figure the catalogue assumes.
research_questions: On the last ten sprinkler jobs, how often were head model, flow and radius already stored before she measured?
How often did the calculated coverage miss a bed she could see, so she reworked the layout by hand?

already_counted.description: Check the coverage figures against the beds and paths she measured. The time sits in that review.

incremental.description: Correct a stored head-flow figure that does not match the head on the bench. The calculation does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the head-flow table is on file and her measures are complete, the sheet does the coverage arithmetic. When the table or the measures are blank, she computes while she designs and the saving is zero. Measuring, checking the ground, marking the layout, and supervising the installation are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List stored rates for this landscaping or groundskeeping service.
Read the service customers asked to have done.
Decide the lowest fee she will accept for that service.
Draft a fee line from those stored rates.
Check the draft fee still matches the service customers named.
Negotiate that fee with the customers.

tasks.design: The {SPREADSHEET} lists the stored labour, material and machine rates, and a draft copies them into a fee line for the service the customers named. She decides the lowest fee, checks that the line matches that service, and negotiates it herself. The draft does not send the fee and does not raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rates lived on a card she had to find, so the opening number was late and easy to misremember.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored rates can be copied into a fee line she checks before she sits down with the customer.
tasks.still_hard: The customer pushes on price. The line does not negotiate.
tasks.human_edge: She decides the lowest fee and says it to the customer. The draft does not.
tasks.altitude: She still decides the floor and still negotiates. She stops hunting a rate card and adding the same rates by hand. She does not gain a right to let the draft offer a fee.

reach.task: Start the job once the fee is agreed.
reach.learn: Which service and which fee she accepted, so a blank rate is not treated as an agreed price.

evidence.claim: Suite MKB calculates quotes for landscapers from work-package rates. The draft copies stored labour, material and machine rates into a fee line. She checks the line and negotiates the fee herself. The advertorial is not a measured time saving, and the draft is not claimed to send an invoice.
The range is a scenario for a quote whose rates are already stored. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The rate card has service name, labour rate, material rate and machine rate. The producer is whoever maintains the rate card, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.

The draft copies only those stored rates onto the service the customers named. It does not apply a discount and it does not set her floor. If a rate is blank, that line stays empty and she names the figure while she negotiates.
Reading the request, deciding the floor, checking the line, and negotiating stay at full time. The shortened steps are listing the stored rates and copying them into the fee line.
The draft writes the fee line and nothing else. It does not send the fee, does not post it to a ledger, and does not raise an alert. She does not file the draft. She speaks the fee.
Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for correcting a stored rate that is out of date before she negotiates. The draft does not send that correction.
unknowns: Whether labour, material and machine rates are stored per service, or only as a yearly card in a drawer.
Who at this firm may go below the rate card, and by how much.
research_questions: On the last ten negotiations, how often were labour, material and machine rates filled for that service before she sat down?
How often did the copied fee line name a different service from the one the customer asked for?

already_counted.description: Check the fee line names the service the customers asked for and does not sit below the floor she set. The time sits in that review.

incremental.description: Correct a stored rate that is out of date before she negotiates. The draft does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When labour, material and machine rates are already stored for the named service, she skips hunting the card and adding those rates by hand. When a rate is blank, the draft leaves the line empty and she negotiates without it, so the saving is zero. Deciding the floor, checking the line, and negotiating are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
